questions.q: Which of the following epidemiological features is the MOST important red flag that should prompt immediate evaluation for systemic infection in a neonate presenting with pustular eruption?
opts: Lesions appearing at 24–48 hours of age in a full-term infant
Pustular eruption in a preterm or low-birth-weight infant (<2500 g)
Female sex with lesions sparing the palms
Blotchy macular erythema in an infant of African descent
questions.exp: Erythema toxicum neonatorum is a disease of healthy infants over 2500 g; pustular eruptions in preterm or low-birth-weight neonates are rare and should always prompt rigorous evaluation for systemic infection (sepsis, congenital infection, herpes simplex). In contrast, ETN in healthy full-term infants requires no investigation beyond clinical assessment and reassurance. Birth weight is therefore the critical epidemiological discriminator.
questions.source: [Paeds Day 1] Transient Neonatal Pustular and Vesicular Eruptions
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: A TINY PRETERM PRISONER (low birth weight) in the dungeon triggers the ALARM BELLS 🔔 for infection—big healthy BARONS (full-term ≥2500 g) in the main hall get ETN as a harmless WELCOME GIFT.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a TORCH pathogen with its distinguishing histopathological finding in infected tissues?
opts: Toxoplasma gondii: Obliterative endarteritis with plasma cell infiltration around blood vessels
Toxoplasma gondii: Crescent-shaped trophozoites with centrally placed nucleus within macrophage cytoplasm
Treponema pallidum: Intracellular pseudocysts visible within multinucleated giant cells
Both pathogens: Identical subacute vasculitis with no distinguishing features
questions.exp: Congenital toxoplasmosis shows characteristic crescent-shaped Toxoplasma gondii trophozoites with a prominent central nucleus within macrophages, whereas congenital syphilis is defined by obliterative endarteritis with plasma cell infiltration. These histopathological findings are pathognomonic for each infection.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: A CRESCENT MOON hangs above a GONDOLA in Venice (Toxo-PLASM-a GONDII), with a central eye peering down from the moon—the parasite's signature crescent nucleus floating inside a macrophage's cozy apartment.

questions.q: An 18-month-old boy is found to have unilateral hypopigmented streaks on his lower extremities only, with no neurological, musculoskeletal, or ophthalmologic abnormalities on detailed examination. What is the most accurate diagnosis?
opts: Hypomelanosis of Ito with atypical systemic presentation
Linear Nevoid Hypopigmentation
Vitiligo with asymmetric distribution
Incontinentia Pigmenti Achromians with incomplete expression
questions.exp: By modern dermatologic definition, the term 'Hypomelanosis of Ito' is strictly reserved for patients with BOTH cutaneous pigmentation defects AND systemic/extracutaneous anomalies involving the CNS, musculoskeletal system, or eyes. When cutaneous hypopigmented findings following Blaschko's lines are present without any internal defects, the correct diagnosis is simply 'Linear Nevoid Hypopigmentation', which represents the cutaneous manifestation alone of the mosaicism.

questions.q: A 3-year-old girl presents with asymmetric whorled patches of hypopigmentation on her trunk and extremities, following the lines of Blaschko. Genetic testing reveals trisomy mosaicism. Which of the following statements about her diagnosis is correct?
opts: The condition is autoimmune-mediated with strong HLA associations and requires routine autoimmune serology
Hypomelanosis of Ito is a descriptive phenotypic term encompassing multiple chromosomal mosaicisms with deficient basal layer melanocytes
The historical term 'Incontinentia Pigmenti Achromians' accurately describes the pathophysiology shared with true Incontinentia Pigmenti
The cutaneous findings alone without systemic involvement confirm the diagnosis of Hypomelanosis of Ito
questions.exp: Hypomelanosis of Ito is a neurocutaneous dysplasia caused by post-zygotic somatic mutations leading to early embryonic mosaicism, not an autoimmune disease. It is a descriptive phenotypic term rather than a single genetic diagnosis, encompassing various chromosomal mosaicisms—notably trisomy mosaicisms—that all manifest with pigment-deficient basal melanocytes. The term 'Incontinentia Pigmenti Achromians' is a historical misnomer because HI lacks the initial vesicular, blistering, and verrucous inflammatory stages that define true IP (Bloch-Sulzberger syndrome) and is genetically/pathophysiologically unrelated to it.

questions.q: A neonate presents with bluish-red infiltrative papules and nodules at birth. Histopathology reveals plaque-like aggregates of nucleated cells and non-nucleated erythrocytes in the reticular dermis. What is the pathophysiological basis of this 'Blueberry Muffin' lesion?
opts: Autoimmune attack on dermal melanocytes leading to pigment deposition
Dermal extramedullary erythropoiesis representing the fetal hematopoietic system's response to severe systemic infectious stress
Inflammatory vasculitis caused by circulating immune complexes deposited in the dermis
Direct microbial invasion and granulomatous inflammation in response to fungal pathogens
questions.exp: The 'Blueberry Muffin' lesion is a hallmark sign of congenital TORCH infections, characterized histologically by dermal extramedullary erythropoiesis rather than inflammation. This represents fetal hematopoietic stress in response to severe systemic infection, not autoimmune or primary inflammatory mechanisms.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture a blueberry muffin OOZING BLOOD CELLS from the baker's oven (reticular dermis)—the fetal body's desperate cry for extra red blood cells during TORCH infection, staining the skin blue-red like a bruised muffin.

questions.q: Which genetic mutation is responsible for congenital haemangiomas (RICH, NICH, and PICH), and what is the mechanism by which it drives prenatal tumour growth?
opts: PTEN loss-of-function mutations causing constitutive PI3K/Akt signalling
Somatic activating GNAQ/GNA11 Gln209 missense mutations leading to MAPK pathway upregulation
CDKN2A inactivation resulting in increased cell cycle progression
FLT4 gain-of-function mutations driving lymphatic endothelial proliferation
questions.exp: Congenital haemangiomas are driven by postzygotic somatic missense mutations in GNAQ and GNA11 genes encoding G-protein alpha-subunits; the characteristic Gln209 substitution constitutively activates MAPK signalling, driving prenatal proliferation. Remarkably, the same Gln209 mutation occurs across all three phenotypes—indicating other unknown factors determine postnatal fate.

questions.q: A newborn with Sturge-Weber syndrome has a port-wine stain over the V1 (ophthalmic) and V2 (maxillary) distributions bilaterally. Which embryological principle best explains why the facial capillary malformation, leptomeningeal angiomatosis, and choroidal involvement often occur together?
opts: The GNAQ mutation occurs in the ectoderm after the 8th week, affecting only dermal vasculature
All three structures derive from endoderm and share a common vascular plexus

The somatic GNAQ mutation arises very early in the anterior neural crest, populating the frontonasal prominence whose neural-crest derivatives form the upper facial vasculature, leptomeninges, and choroid
Postnatal angiogenesis in response to chronic hypoxia links the three vascular territories
questions.exp: The pathogenesis of the Sturge-Weber triad is explained by the timing and location of the somatic GNAQ mutation within the anterior neural crest or cephalic mesenchyme. This early clonal event populates the neural-crest–derived mural cells that form the facial cutaneous vasculature, leptomeningeal vasculature, and ocular choroid simultaneously, producing the characteristic constellation of findings.

questions.q: A 2-month-old boy presents with a port-wine stain over the left forehead and upper eyelid. His parents are concerned about future complications. Which genetic mechanism underlies Sturge-Weber syndrome?
opts: Autosomal dominant inheritance from an affected parent
Somatic postzygotic GNAQ mutation (c.548G>A; p.Arg183Gln) causing mosaic disease
Germline mutation in GNA11 transmitted through maternal lineage
X-linked recessive inheritance with variable expression in females
questions.exp: Sturge-Weber syndrome is a non-inherited neurocutaneous disorder caused by a somatic activating missense mutation in GNAQ that occurs early in the anterior neural crest after fertilization. Because the mutation is postzygotic and confined to affected tissue, there is no germline transmission and no inheritance pattern.

questions.q: A 6-year-old girl with alopecia areata is found to have the HLA-DRB1*0401 and HLA-DQB1*0301 genotypes. What is the clinical significance of these specific HLA associations?
opts: These alleles are protective markers that predict a favorable prognosis and complete spontaneous remission within 1 year
These alleles indicate a general susceptibility to AA in any individual, with no prognostic implications
These alleles are specific genetic markers for severe, longstanding alopecia totalis or universalis
These alleles are exclusively found in pediatric-onset AA and do not occur in adults
questions.exp:
While HLA-DQB1*03 (DQ3) is a general susceptibility marker for all forms of alopecia areata, the specific alleles HLA-DRB1*0401 (DR4) and HLA-DQB1*0301 (DQ7) are associated with severe, longstanding disease phenotypes including alopecia totalis and universalis. These markers have prognostic significance in predicting more extensive and persistent hair loss.
🏰 Palace: Imagine DR4 and DQ7 as DARK RED flags (DR4 = DaRk Red) flying above a CASTLE FORTRESS (severe disease stronghold)—only the most fortified, severe cases fly these menacing flags.
questions.source: [paeds Day 28] Alopecia areata in children + JAKi

questions.q: A 2-week-old male presents with a fully formed vascular tumour on his leg that was present at birth. The lesion measures 3 cm in diameter, is bright red with peripheral pallor, and the parents report it appears to be flattening slightly. Immunohistochemistry shows GLUT1-negative staining. Based on the clinical presentation and natural history, which congenital haemangioma subtype is most likely?
opts: NICH (Non-Involuting Congenital Haemangioma)
RICH (Rapidly Involuting Congenital Haemangioma)
Infantile haemangioma
PICH (Partially Involuting Congenital Haemangioma)
questions.exp: RICH presents as a fully formed lesion at birth with rapid postnatal involution beginning within days to weeks, typically complete by 14 months—matching this clinical scenario. The GLUT1-negative status and presence at birth exclude infantile haemangioma. NICH would persist without regression, and PICH shows incomplete involution with residual lesions.

questions.q: A 3-week-old Black neonate presents with a poorly circumscribed, slate-gray macular patch over the lumbosacral region. On dermoscopy, you observe dendritic melanocytes arranged parallel to the skin surface within the mid and lower reticular dermis. What is the primary optical mechanism responsible for the characteristic bluish hue of this lesion?
opts: Rayleigh scattering of longer wavelengths by superficial epidermal keratin
Tyndall effect—selective scattering of shorter blue light wavelengths by deep dermal melanin back to the observer's eye
Melanin absorption of red and infrared light with reflectance of blue light
Optical diffraction through regularly spaced collagen bundles in the reticular dermis
questions.exp: The characteristic bluish-gray color of a Mongolian spot is caused by the Tyndall effect, where shorter blue light wavelengths are preferentially scattered by melanin granules located deep in the dermis and reflected back to the observer's eye. Longer wavelengths are absorbed by the deeper melanin, creating the optical illusion of a blue lesion rather than the true brown color of melanin. This optical principle is fundamental to understanding why dermal melanocytosis appears blue rather than brown.

questions.q: A 4-year-old child of Southeast Asian descent presents with extensive, dark Mongolian spots involving the trunk, shoulders, and extremities in a confetti-like pattern that has been progressively darkening over the past year. The parents report normal development but mild coarsening of facial features. Which of the following inborn errors of metabolism should be prioritized in the differential diagnosis?
opts: Acute intermittent porphyria with late-onset cutaneous manifestations
Lysosomal storage diseases such as Hurler's disease (MPS I), Hunter's disease (MPS II), and GM1 gangliosidosis type 1
Neurofibromatosis type 1 with segmental involvement
X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with secondary pigmentation
questions.exp: Extensive, dark, and progressive Mongolian spots extending beyond the lumbosacral region with confetti-like appearance are a major cutaneous red flag for underlying inborn errors of metabolism, particularly lysosomal storage diseases including Hurler's disease, Hunter's disease, GM1 gangliosidosis type 1, and Niemann-Pick disease. These metabolic disorders are associated with hepatosplenomegaly, coarsening of features, developmental delay, and progressive systemic involvement. The combination of extensive dermal melanocytosis with progressive course and subtle systemic signs should prompt urgent metabolic evaluation.

questions.q: A 3-week-old neonate presents with profuse, purulent, blood-tinged nasal discharge that began in the first week of life. The mother received no antenatal care. Which of the following statements about this clinical presentation is correct?
opts: This finding (snuffles) is pathognomonic for congenital syphilis and the discharge is non-infectious
Snuffles typically appears after 8 weeks of life and represents late congenital syphilis
Snuffles is often the first symptom of early congenital syphilis, presenting in the first weeks of life with highly infectious spirochete-laden discharge
Snuffles in congenital syphilis primarily affects the lower respiratory tract with bronchospasm
questions.exp: Snuffles (syphilitic rhinitis) is the most characteristic early presentation of congenital syphilis, occurring in the first weeks of life as a profuse, watery nasal discharge that becomes purulent and blood-tinged. The discharge is teeming with Treponema pallidum spirochetes and highly infectious. Most symptomatic infants develop signs between 3-8 weeks of life, which classifies the condition as early congenital syphilis (< 2 years).
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture a SNUFFLING BABY DRAGON (snuffles) breathing BLOODY GOOP through its NOSE PORTAL, with glowing SPIROCHETES (treponemes) dancing like fireflies in the infectious mucus—a medieval castle's first warning of infection.

questions.q: An 18-month-old child from Singapore presents with severe brainstem encephalitis, acute flaccid paralysis, and pulmonary edema following an initial mucocutaneous illness resembling hand-foot-and-mouth disease. The parents report a prodrome of vesicles on the palms and soles. Which enterovirus serotype is most likely responsible for this severe neurologic phenotype?
opts: Coxsackievirus A16
Coxsackievirus A6
Enterovirus 71
Echovirus type 5
questions.exp: Enterovirus 71 (EV-A71) is the highly virulent subtype that causes severe, potentially fatal systemic complications including brainstem encephalitis, encephalomyelitis, acute flaccid paralysis, and fatal pulmonary edema and hemorrhage. This virus exhibits dangerous tropism for the CNS and cardiopulmonary tissues. Massive epidemics of EV71 have recurrently occurred in the Asia-Pacific region since the late 1990s.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: EV71's EVIL NUMBER (7+1=8, death's infinity loop) sends the virus UP a twisted brainstem STAIRCASE in the castle tower, where it chokes the LUNGS with hemorrhagic fog—only EV71 dares enter the CNS throne room; CVA16 stays safely in the outer HAND-FOOT courtyard.

questions.q: Which cell-surface receptor is aberrantly expressed on clonally proliferating mast cells in mastocytosis but is strictly absent on normal reactive mast cells?
opts: CD34 and CD38
CD25 and/or CD2
CD56 and CD57
HLA-DR and CD11c
questions.exp: Clonally aberrant mast cells in mastocytosis uniquely express CD25 and/or CD2, which are not present on normal reactive mast cells. These markers, along with KIT (CD117) overexpression, help distinguish neoplastic mast cell proliferation from benign reactive mast cell infiltration. This immunophenotypic profile is crucial for diagnosis.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: In the castle's DEFECTIVE WORKSHOP, a CLOWN (CD25/CD2) hands out BROKEN TOOLS (aberrant mast cells) while NORMAL BUILDERS (reactive mast cells) refuse them—the clown's gift is the neoplastic signature!

questions.q: A 5-year-old girl with a clinical diagnosis of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is being evaluated for genetic counseling. Her parents ask whether she might instead have Legius syndrome given that both conditions present with café-au-lait macules and intertriginous freckling. Which clinical or investigation finding would MOST reliably distinguish NF1 from Legius syndrome?
opts: Presence of ≥6 café-au-lait macules measuring >5 mm in prepubertal individuals
Detection of giant melanosomes on skin biopsy histopathology
Development of axillary and inguinal freckling (Crowe's sign)
Identification of pigmented iris hamartomas (Lisch nodules) and/or optic pathway gliomas on ophthalmologic examination
questions.exp: While both NF1 and Legius syndrome (caused by SPRED1 mutations) present with multiple café-au-lait macules and intertriginous freckling in early childhood, Legius syndrome crucially NEVER develops neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, or CNS tumors. The presence of Lisch nodules or optic gliomas definitively excludes Legius syndrome and confirms the NF1 diagnosis. Options A–C are non-specific features shared by both conditions.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine LISCH NODULES as GLOWING IRIS JEWELS only worn by the TRUE VON RECKLINGHAUSEN QUEEN—Legius pretenders dress identically but their eyes remain bare and their optic pathways forever tumour-free.

questions.q: A 5-year-old girl with Rothmund-Thomson syndrome presents with progressive poikiloderma and bilateral cataracts requiring early surgical intervention. Genetic testing reveals ANAPC1 mutations. What is the most significant prognostic difference compared to RECQL4-mutated disease?
opts: Absence of skeletal abnormalities
Significantly increased risk of osteosarcoma and cutaneous malignancies
No increased incidence of malignancy
Earlier onset of poikiloderma by 2–3 years
questions.exp: Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type I (ANAPC1 mutations) is distinguished by a high incidence of juvenile cataracts—the original Rothmund presentation—but crucially exhibits NO increased incidence of malignancy, contrasting sharply with RECQL4-driven Type II disease which carries a 32% osteosarcoma risk. This cancer-sparing rule is the key discriminating prognostic feature.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture CATARACTS (cloudy eye lenses) sitting in a SAFE (ANAPCing the cell cycle safely) inside a tumor-free castle tower—Type I patients get cloudy eyes but DODGE the cancer bullet, unlike their Type II cousins in the malignancy tower next door.

questions.q: A 6-year-old boy presents with early-onset poikiloderma, hypoplastic thumbs, and absent radii. Genetic testing reveals compound heterozygous mutations in the RECQL4 gene. What is his estimated lifetime risk of osteosarcoma?
questions.exp: Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type II, caused by RECQL4 mutations, is characterized by severe skeletal abnormalities (radial ray defects) and a distinctive 32% risk of osteosarcoma—the hallmark malignancy discriminating feature of this subtype. This profound malignancy predisposition reflects the critical role of RECQL4 helicase in DNA replication and repair.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine a giant RADIAL THUMB (32 bones in the hand) BREAKING into FRAGMENTS shaped like OSTEOSARC (bone-sarcoma eggs) scattered across 32 castle towers—one crumbling tower per percentage point of malignancy risk in RECQL4 Type II patients.

questions.q: A 14-year-old boy presents with a 5 mm brown nevus on his upper back surrounded by a well-demarcated zone of completely depigmented skin. Histology shows dense CD8+ lymphocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis with destruction of nevus cells. Which immunological axis is primarily responsible for this targeted melanocyte destruction?
opts: IL-4 and STAT6 signaling in Th2 cells
CXCL10–CXCR3 chemokine axis driving CD8+ T-cell infiltration
TNF-α and IL-17 from Th17 lymphocytes
IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation
questions.exp:
Halo nevus is a CD8+ T-cell-mediated autoimmune process against melanocytes, driven specifically by the CXCL10–CXCR3 chemokine receptor–ligand axis—the same pathway implicated in vitiligo pathogenesis. This interferon-gamma–inducible axis recruits cytotoxic lymphocytes that recognize shared melanocytic antigens. Circulating anti-melanoma antibodies further confirm the autoimmune nature of this destruction.
🏰 Palace: Imagine a CASTLE GUARD (CXCL10–CXCR3) standing at the GATE, ringing a bell (interferon-gamma) that summons CD8+ ASSASSINS through the moat to destroy the BROWN NEVUS FORTRESS—just like they do to vitiligo cells in the royal treasury next door.

questions.q: A 7-year-old girl presents with sharply demarcated, symmetrical erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales on her extensor surfaces. Histopathology reveals marked epidermal acanthosis with regular elongation of rete ridges, absent granular layer, and confluent parakeratosis. Which histological finding would be MOST specific for confirming the diagnosis of psoriasis?
opts: Regular, uniform elongation of rete ridges with hypogranulosis
Munro microabscesses and spongiform pustules of Kogoj
Dilated, tortuous papillary dermal capillaries alone
Prominent dermal fibrosis with reduced vascularity
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (localized neutrophil collections in the stratum corneum) and spongiform pustules of Kogoj (in the upper spinous layer) are the pathognomonic histological features of psoriasis. While acanthosis and hypogranulosis are characteristic, the presence of these neutrophilic collections is absolutely diagnostic. The note explicitly states these are 'localized collections of neutrophils within the epidermis' that are 'absolute pathognomonic features.'
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture KOGOJ (a stern warrior) spearing NEUTROPHILS like tiny soldiers stacked in the castle's UPPER SPINOUS TOWER, while MUNRO (a guard) guards the STRATUM CORNEUM gate below with his microabscess cannons—these are the TWO ROYAL SEALS proving psoriasis rules the kingdom.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl with Turner syndrome is found to have multiple halo nevi on her trunk. Which HLA allele is specifically associated with this increased prevalence of halo nevi in Turner syndrome?
opts: HLA-B27
HLA-CW6
HLA-DQ2
HLA-DR3
questions.exp:
Halo nevi occur with markedly increased frequency (18% prevalence) in Turner syndrome patients compared to the general population (1%), and this association is specifically linked to the HLA-CW6 allele. While halo nevi are typically sporadic, Turner syndrome represents a critical genetic risk factor that amplifies the autoimmune predisposition to melanocyte destruction. This HLA association underscores the immunogenetic basis of the condition.
🏰 Palace: In the TURNER CASTLE (Turner syndrome), the HLA-CW6 FLAG flies from the turret—raise that FLAG (CW6) and watch HALO HALOS (18% prevalence) bloom on the trunk walls like a demarcation line between the kingdom and the invading immune army.

questions.q: A 5-year-old boy with a recent streptococcal pharyngitis develops numerous small, drop-shaped erythematous lesions with fine scales scattered across his trunk and proximal limbs over 2–3 weeks. Genetic testing reveals HLA-Cw6 positivity. What is the most likely psoriasis subtype in this child?
opts: Plaque psoriasis (psoriasis vulgaris)
Guttate psoriasis
Palmoplantar psoriasis
Scalp psoriasis with corona psoriatica
questions.exp: Guttate psoriasis is the second most common variant in childhood (6.4–44% of cases) and is heavily triggered by streptococcal infection, particularly pharyngitis. The clinical presentation of drop-shaped (guttate) lesions following a streptococcal trigger in a child strongly suggests this variant. Guttate psoriasis also carries the absolute strongest association with HLA-Cw6 of all psoriasis variants.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine TINY WATER DROPLETS (guttae = drops) cascading from a STREP THROAT MONSTER in the castle courtyard, each droplet landing as a small red lesion on the walls—GUTTATE psoriasis is triggered by STREP like water follows gravity.

questions.q: A pregnant woman at 15 weeks gestation is diagnosed with primary syphilis. She is treated adequately with penicillin before 18 weeks of pregnancy. Which statement best explains why this timing of treatment is critical in preventing fetal complications?
opts: The placental barrier becomes impermeable after 18 weeks, preventing all transplacental transmission

Maternal treatment before 16-18 weeks prevents fetal infection because the fetus lacks immunocompetence and cannot mount the inflammatory response necessary to cause tissue destruction and irreversible stigmata
Penicillin cannot cross the placenta after 18 weeks of gestation
Treponema pallidum cannot infect the fetus before 20 weeks of gestation
questions.exp: The fetus does not achieve full immunocompetence until approximately 18-20 weeks of gestation. Before this time, the characteristic inflammatory tissue destruction and necrosis of syphilis do not occur, even if infection is present. Therefore, adequate maternal penicillin treatment before 16-18 weeks almost always prevents fetal infection and subsequent irreversible stigmata by treating the mother before fetal immunity develops enough to cause tissue damage.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine a SLEEPING BABY (immature fetus) in a golden CRIB guarded by a CLOCK striking 18—the PENICILLIN SWORD must enter before the clock chimes, or the INFLAMMATORY DRAGON awakens and leaves permanent scars on the castle walls.

questions.q: A 7-year-old boy presents with sudden onset of a single round patch of hair loss on the scalp. On examination, you observe smooth, completely hairless skin with no scaling or erythema. At the periphery of the patch, several hairs are noted to be narrower at the base and wider distally. Which of the following best explains why this child retains the potential for complete hair regrowth despite active hair loss?
opts: The inflammatory infiltrate destroys the dermal papilla permanently, but stem cells in the infundibulum can differentiate into new follicles
The autoimmune attack is localized to the peribulbar region of anagen hairs while the bulge region (upper follicular stem cell reservoir) is spared
The hair matrix cells are temporarily suppressed but the sebaceous gland epithelium can transdifferentiate into new hair-producing cells
Melanocyte-associated antigens are the sole target, so non-pigmented hairs remain unaffected and can serve as the source of regrowth
questions.exp:
Alopecia areata is non-cicatricial because the immune attack is strictly localized to the peribulbar region of the anagen hair follicle, while the bulge region (the upper follicular stem cell reservoir) is completely spared. This anatomical preservation of the stem cell niche is why hair retains full potential to regrow even years later, distinguishing AA from scarring alopecias.
🏰 Palace: Picture a CASTLE BULGE (bulge region) at the TOP of a tall tower, protected by guards while INVADERS (lymphocytes) swarm the LOWER PERIBULBAR DUNGEON below—the treasure (stem cells) stays safe.
questions.source: [paeds Day 28] Alopecia areata in children + JAKi

questions.q: A 3-year-old boy presents with 8 well-circumscribed, uniformly pigmented brown patches on his trunk and limbs, ranging from 0.8–1.2 cm in diameter. His parents report they were not visible at birth but became apparent during the first 6 months of life. Physical examination reveals axillary freckling and small flesh-colored papules on his chest. Histopathology shows normal melanocyte numbers in the basal layer but marked melanin hyperpigmentation in keratinocytes with giant melanosomes. Which genetic pathway is most likely disrupted?
opts: Autoimmune-mediated loss of melanocytes via anti-PMEL17 antibodies
Constitutive activation of the Ras-MAPK intracellular signaling pathway
Inflammatory cytokine cascade leading to epidermal CD8+ T-cell infiltration
HLA-B27-associated immune receptor dysfunction
questions.exp: Café-au-lait macules, particularly when syndromic (≥6 lesions with axillary freckling and neurofibromas), are driven by autosomal dominant mutations in genes regulating the Ras-MAPK pathway—most commonly NF1 (neurofibromin). This is strictly a genetic pigmentary disorder, NOT an autoimmune, inflammatory, or HLA-associated condition. The histological finding of giant melanosomes in the setting of Ras-MAPK dysregulation is pathognomonic for neurofibromatosis-spectrum disease.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture Ras proteins as TINY MAPK WORKERS building GIANT CHOCOLATE (melanin) PILLARS in the castle—the blueprint (NF1 gene) is broken, so they overproduce forever, creating the characteristic giant melanosomes.

questions.q: A 3-year-old boy presents with polymorphic reddish-brown macules and papules on his trunk and thighs. Stroking a lesion produces immediate whealing and erythema. Histopathology shows a 40-fold increase in mast cells primarily in the papillary dermis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Cutaneous mastocytosis, maculopapular type (urticaria pigmentosa)
Mastocytoma of skin
Telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans
Systemic mastocytosis with skin involvement
questions.exp: Maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis (MPCM/urticaria pigmentosa) is the most common form of mastocytosis, classically presenting with polymorphic lesions in children that often resolve by adolescence. The positive Darier's sign (immediate whealing upon stroking) and papillary dermal infiltration are pathognomonic findings. The 40-fold increase in mast cells on histology is characteristic of this subtype.

questions.q: A 2-day-old full-term neonate presents with scattered erythematous macules and firm 1–3 mm pustules on the cheeks, chest and trunk. The lesions spare the palms and soles. Smear cytology reveals a predominance of eosinophils with occasional neutrophils; Gram stain and culture are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Neonatal herpes simplex infection
Erythema toxicum neonatorum
Congenital varicella
Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
questions.exp: The clinical presentation—benign transient pustules sparing palms/soles in a healthy full-term infant at 24–48 hours of life with sterile eosinophil-predominant smear cytology—is pathognomonic for erythema toxicum neonatorum (ETN). Despite its name, ETN is not toxic and not infectious; it represents a localised innate-immune response to commensal skin microbes colonising the pilosebaceous unit. Herpes and varicella present with vesicles, systemic symptoms and positive virology; toxic shock syndrome causes systemic toxicity absent here.
questions.source: [Paeds Day 1] Transient Neonatal Pustular and Vesicular Eruptions
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: A full-term NEWBORN (2 days old) sits at the castle ENTRANCE collecting EOSINOPHILS in a FLEA-BITTEN coat—but the DOORMAN (palms/soles) blocks entry; ETN = INNOCENT intruder, not a TOXIC VILLAIN.

questions.q: A 4-year-old boy presents with a 2-day history of low-grade fever, malaise, and painful ulcers on his tongue and buccal mucosa with erythematous halos. Two days later, he develops a non-pruritic exanthem on his palms and soles. Examination reveals characteristic elliptical vesicles with their long axes running parallel to the natural skin lines. A skin biopsy is performed. Which of the following histological findings would help distinguish this condition from herpes simplex virus infection?
opts: Presence of multinucleated giant cells and viral inclusion bodies
Absence of viral inclusion bodies and multinucleated giant cells
Acantholysis with loss of intercellular connections
Subepidermal bulla with intact basal layer
questions.exp: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease histology shows intraepidermal vesicles with vacuolar degeneration and keratinocyte necrosis, but crucially lacks viral inclusion bodies and multinucleated giant cells—findings that would be present in herpes simplex or varicella infections. This absence is a key diagnostic differentiator on histopathology.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture a castle WITHOUT guards (no inclusion bodies) and WITHOUT mirror-image giant soldiers (no multinucleated giant cells)—only regular dermal knights marching around empty HFMD hallways, while HSV knights carry golden viral badges and cloned warrior twins (inclusions + multinucleates) down the herpes wing.
